Sushi grade fish is actually not that hard to get, although your normal grocery store likely won't have it. Foodie/gourmet grocers sometimes have it and can usually get it if you ask. If you have a distributor in the area that sells to the public, that's probably the best way.

In the end, it was really more of a novelty and I enjoy it as a one in a while restaurant experience more than making it for myself regularly.

I also read that you need a rice cooker that specifically has a sushi rice setting. Then i started looking at prices for such cookers and found they all are in the $100 plus range. Did you do it on the stovetop?

You do not need a special rice cooker (or any rice cooker). You can cook it on the stove top.

Just read up on tips and tricks for getting it right. e.g. using a large flat wooden (not metal) surface for spreading the rice and seasoning it with the vinegar.
Yeah, and I think that was part of the problem.

You can make rice in whatever you have. I used a pot on the stove top for the longest time until someone gave me a rice cooker. I usually make my rice with 3 cups dry and rinse until the water is clear ish. Then after its cooked I gently mix in 1/4 cup rice wine vinegar and 1/4 cup white sugar.

You can achieve more than decent results your first time. I've made it maybe half a dozen times. My skills improved each time - but even the first time was delicious. It is expensive to buy all the little things that make it so wonderful and it is a lot of prep work but you can make very good tasting stuff with just a bit of practice.

You should be able to find high quality sushi fish at most Japanese markets (if there is one near you). In my town the company that supplies most of the sushi restaurants also operates their own fish market - so you can get pretty much the same fish.
